description:
A double-height contemporary living room photographed at a slightly elevated standing position — approximately six to seven feet — centered symmetrically on the rear fireplace wall, framing the full two-story room volume with wide-angle coverage. The camera is level, capturing the full height from floor to upper mezzanine level above.

The room is entirely executed in warm white and pale sand tones — a thoroughly monochromatic palette of creamy plaster, off-white linen upholstery, light oak plank flooring, and large-format pale limestone or concrete wall cladding. The rear wall, which serves as the fireplace surround, is clad floor-to-ceiling in oversized rectangular stone-look panels in ivory with barely-there grey veining, with the fireplace opening and a long horizontal gas flame insert low in the surround. A recessed linear reveal in the wall creates a subtle architectural frame around the fireplace panel.

A large sectional sofa in warm cream-white linen fills the left foreground, paired with a round light concrete or travertine coffee table on a pale area rug. A second sofa is partially visible at the right foreground. The space beyond through floor-to-ceiling glazed black-framed sliding panels on the right reveals an exterior terrace or garden with further seating.

On the upper level, a mezzanine or gallery walkway with open railing or low parapet runs across the left side. Warm amber LED strips line the ceiling perimeter and mezzanine soffits in a deep recessed channel, creating bands of warm ambient light layered against the cool neutral walls. Sheer warm cream curtains frame the right glass wall.

The overall atmosphere is serene, minimal, and gallery-white — an aspirational contemporary family home with breathtaking volume.
